title: Every finitely branching level tree carries a sequence of ordered partitions with uniform successor numbers

standard_prerequisites.name: The levels L_k of a tree with omega levels, all finite, and the successor set of a node
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Set up in the paragraphs preceding the counted statement (ending at source line 525)

standard_prerequisites.name: A sequence of natural numbers in which every number occurs infinitely often, and the eventual constancy of a refining sequence of partitions of a finite set
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Used inside the counted proof at lines 532 and 546-547
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the schedule of refinements and the reason the refining sequences stabilise.

core_obligations: Fix the schedule and the refining sequences: use a sequence (k_n) in which every natural number occurs infinitely often, and build partitions pi_k^n of each level L_k, refining as n grows, starting from the trivial one-piece partition (proof lines 532-536).

Perform one refinement: at stage n only the level k_n is refined, by grouping the nodes x of L_k according to the sequence of intersection sizes |X cap succ(x)| for X in the current partition of the next level, and then taking the least common refinement with the previous partition and extending the order so that it remains convex (proof lines 538-544).

Pass to the limit: because each refining sequence of partitions of a finite set is eventually constant, the pi_k^n stabilise at some pi_k, and at the limit the equivalence relation used in the refinement is trivial on each piece (proof lines 546-548).

Read off uniformity: consequently, for X in pi_k the whole sequence (|Y cap succ(x)| : Y in pi_{k+1}) is the same for every x in X, so each x in X has the same total number of successors and the same number in each Y, which is the number n(X,Y) (proof lines 548-551).
proof_roadmap: Set up refining sequences of ordered partitions scheduled along a sequence hitting every level infinitely often, and refine one level at each stage (proof lines 532-544).
Use eventual constancy on finite levels to see that the refinement relation becomes trivial on each piece, which forces the successor counts to be uniform (proof lines 546-551).
difficulty_reason: The theorem produces, for any tree with omega finite levels, a sequence of ordered partitions of its levels such that between consecutive levels the number of successors of a node inside a given piece is the same for all nodes of the piece (statement lines 527-530). The proof runs refinements of the partitions of each level along a schedule in which every level is treated infinitely often, refining one level at a stage by grouping nodes according to the vector of intersection sizes with the pieces of the next level, and ordering the pieces so that each previous piece splits into consecutive parts (proof lines 532-544). The step that carries the content is the limit argument: since each level is finite the refining sequences stabilise, and at the stable stage the grouping relation has become trivial on every piece, which is exactly what makes the successor counts uniform (proof lines 546-551). H2.
